details: The Federal Reserve is widely expected to keep interest rates steady at its current range of 3.50%-3.75% during its upcoming Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on June 16-17. However, strong May employment data and persistent inflation, with the US Consumer Price Index (CPI) reaching 4.2% year-over-year and Producer Price Index (PPI) surging to 6.5% year-over-year, are signaling a potentially more hawkish stance from new Chair Kevin Warsh. Markets are increasingly anticipating a rate hike by year-end instead of previously hoped-for cuts, which would continue to serve as a headwind for risk assets, including cryptocurrencies.
sourceName: Crypto Briefing (citing JPMorgan), Mohamed A. El-Erian (Substack)
title: Fed Maintains Rates but Signals Hawkish Outlook Amid High Inflation

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) raised its three key interest rates by 25 basis points, effective June 17, 2026. This marks the first rate hike since 2023 and is a direct response to persistent inflation, largely driven by the conflict in the Middle East. The ECB projects headline inflation to average 3.0% in 2026 and has consequently revised its economic growth forecasts for both 2026 and 2027 downward. Policymakers have also indicated that further rate increases, possibly in July, remain a strong possibility.
title: ECB Raises Key Interest Rates by 25 BPS Amid Inflationary Pressures

details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has voiced concerns regarding the growing adoption of US dollar-denominated stablecoins in Nigeria. In its "2026 Article IV Consultation Staff Country Report on Nigeria," the IMF identified potential risks to monetary sovereignty, capital flow management, financial stability, and integrity. The report highlights the possibility of "digital dollarisation" occurring outside the country's formal financial system, which could prompt increased regulatory scrutiny and impact wider crypto adoption in emerging markets.
title: IMF Highlights Monetary Risks from Rising Stablecoin Use in Nigeria

details: The cryptocurrency market has experienced significant volatility, with $142 million in crypto futures liquidations occurring within a 24-hour period around June 14, primarily affecting Bitcoin and Ethereum. This downturn comes amidst broader macroeconomic headwinds, including persistent inflation and increasingly hawkish signals from central banks, which are dampening investor demand for risk assets. Bitcoin ETF flows have shown net outflows, and the Crypto Fear and Greed Index currently sits in "extreme fear" territory, reflecting cautious market sentiment despite Bitcoin recently seeing a slight uptick to over $64,500.
title: Crypto Market Volatile, $142M Liquidated Amid Macro Headwinds
